moat_against: Hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, GCP) outscale on price, custom silicon and bundled credits; niche rivals Vultr and Akamai/Linode sell the same commodity compute
Low switching costs on core droplets/compute; SMB and developer customers are price-sensitive
ROIC history weak: roic_proxy 12.2% in FY2025 is the first double-digit print, after 1.0% in 2023 and negative prints in 2020-22
Gross margin compressing as GPU/AI mix rises: 61.4% in Q1 2025 to 55.0% in Q2 2026 (fundamentals.json quarterly)
No proprietary silicon, network scale or owned consumer distribution
moat_for: Developer brand, simplicity and predictable pricing vs hyperscaler complexity and egress fees
Managed platform layer (Kubernetes, databases, inference engine) — 85% of AI-customer ARR from inference + core cloud rather than bare metal
Large-cohort growth and stickiness: $1M+ customer ARR +214% YoY in Q2 2026, record $93M incremental ARR in the quarter
Self-serve acquisition economics — CAC payback 9.3 months reported in Q1 2026 coverage
moat_justification: Developer brand, simplicity and predictable pricing win SMB/digital-native workloads from hyperscalers, and the managed platform layer is getting stickier (85% of AI-customer ARR from inference + core cloud, not bare metal) — but compute is commodity with low switching costs, AWS/Azure/GCP outscale it, gross margin is compressing on GPU mix (about 61% in Q1 2025 to 55.0% in Q2 2026), and ROIC (roic_proxy in fundamentals.json) only reached 12.2% in FY2025 after -14.3% / -2.7% / -1.5% / 1.0% in 2020-23 and 9.2% in 2024 — no through-cycle proof of returns above the cost of capital, so no score above the moderate band.
name: DigitalOcean Holdings, Inc.
one_liner: Real AI-inference growth story with a narrow moat 5/10 — but at $97.50 the price pays for more than the super-bull case: weighted IRR 6.1%, weighted IV@15% $22.85, and it clears a 15% hurdle only below ~$22.85.
